scenario: Scenario 1: Overseer CREATE paths that never supply coreNodeName (non-legacy SPLITSHARD)
notes: The primary result is MC-1, a 6-state TargetSafe counterexample. An operator sends the supported Collections API call CLUSTERPROP legacyCloud=false, and the Overseer writes /clusterprops.json. On a later SPLITSHARD, OverseerCollectionProcessor.splitShard sends the sub-shard leader CoreAdmin CREATE without a coreNodeName (OCP:1339-1347). The receiving node's handleCreateAction reads non-legacy mode live from ZooKeeper, sees coreNodeName == null, and throws at CoreAdminHandler.java:560. No crash, partition, timeout or race is needed; the mechanism is a supported configuration setting. This was reproduced on the unmodified base commit 6e6ca4a by repro/SpeculaMC1SplitNonLegacyTest.java, a ShardSplitTest#testDistribSearch variant in solr/core that uses only public CLUSTERPROP and SPLITSHARD calls, under seeds 1A2B3C4D and DEADBEEF. The CAH:560 frame appears in repro/MC-1.log lines 2502 and 2539 and in repro/MC-1.seed2.log. Two other reproduced entries also reach the same line. MC-2 (Scenario 2, MC_hunt_legacy_flip_race.cfg, mechanism INTERLEAVING) is a legacyCloud flip that lands between the OCP's read and the receiver's live read during ADDREPLICA or CREATE collection; see repro/test_bugMC-2_SpeculaAdhocMC2Test.java and the repro/MC-2_*.log files. CR-1 comes from code review and was not model-checked; CREATESHARD and MIGRATE send a CREATE without coreNodeName under legacyCloud=false (repro/test_bugCR-1_SpeculaCR1NonLegacyCreateShardMigrateTest.java, repro/CR-1-run-*.log). MC.cfg without CLUSTERPROP holds TargetSafe over its complete state space (4,366 distinct states, diameter 42), which matches the passing workload. All three traces pass trace validation: workload, variant_concurrent and variant_rounds.
